record.original_question: Can Einstein gravity be made compatible with modern dynamical mass generation and traceless conformal energy-momentum tensors? If microscopic strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions are responsible for particle and macroscopic masses, and if conformal invariant theories have kinematically traceless energy-momentum tensors, why should such matter be equated to the non-conformal, non-traceless Einstein tensor, and what should replace the non-dynamical Planck mass?

evidence.quote: One final loose end in the standard theory is in our understanding not of the gravitational side of the equation of motion but rather in our understanding of the energy-momentum side.

Unlike the situation that existed in Einstein’s time, we no longer regard mass as being kinematical, but rather it is now thought of as being dynamically induced in theories in which there are no fundamental scales at the level of the action at all, with all scales being induced dynamically in the vacuum; and indeed this motivated Mannheim and Kazanas to study conformal gravity in the first place.
In conformal invariant theories the energy-momentum tensor is kinematically traceless.

Consequently it is somewhat difficult to understand why any such energy-momentum tensor should be set equal to the non-conformal invariant, non-traceless Einstein tensor as would be required by Eq. (10).

However, one prominent gravitational mass, the Planck mass, is not dynamical. We are thus led naturally to consider removing it from physics; and thus the apparent lack of compatibility between the Einstein theory and current ideas on mass and the structure of the other fundamental interactions represents another loose end for the Einstein theory, one which could even hinder a possible unification of gravity with the other interactions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In standard Einstein gravity the field equation has the form G_{\mu
u} = -8\pi G\, T_{\mu
u}, where G_{\mu
u} = R_{\mu
u} - 	frac{1}{2} g_{\mu
u} R is the Einstein tensor associated to a Lorentzian metric g_{\mu
u}, G is Newton's constant (equivalently, a fixed Planck mass scale M_P = G^{-1/2} appears in the action S_{EH} = (16\pi G)^{-1}\int R\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x), and T_{\mu
u} is the energy-momentum tensor of the matter fields. The Einstein tensor satisfies g^{\mu
u} G_{\mu
u} = -R, which is generically nonzero, so G_{\mu
u} is neither conformally invariant nor traceless.

In modern microscopic descriptions of strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions, the masses of elementary particles and of macroscopic bodies are not put in by hand as kinematical parameters but are generated dynamically, e.g. by spontaneous symmetry breaking of an underlying locally conformal-invariant action that contains no fundamental mass scales. For such a locally conformal-invariant matter theory the canonically improved energy-momentum tensor T_{\mu
u} is kinematically traceless: g^{\mu
u} T_{\mu
u} = 0 as an identity (not merely as a consequence of the matter equations of motion).

Problem. Construct a classical theory of gravity coupled to matter satisfying all of the following:

(i) The matter sector is described by a locally conformally invariant action with no fundamental mass scales, so that its energy-momentum tensor T_{\mu
u} is identically traceless and all particle and macroscopic mass scales arise from dynamical symmetry breaking in the vacuum.

(ii) The gravitational field equation consistently equates (a tensor built from the metric to) this traceless, conformally covariant T_{\mu
u}, in a manner compatible with the kinematic tracelessness of T_{\mu
u} (i.e. the geometric side of the equation must itself be traceless, or be made so by the same dynamical symmetry-breaking mechanism that generates particle masses).

(iii) The fixed, non-dynamical Planck mass M_P of Einstein gravity is replaced by a scale generated dynamically in the vacuum, so that Newton's constant emerges from the same symmetry-breaking mechanism that gives particles their masses.

(iv) In an appropriate limit or regime, the theory reproduces the empirically successful predictions of Einstein gravity (solar-system tests, Newtonian limit, etc.).

Determine whether such a theory exists, and if so identify what should replace the Einstein tensor G_{\mu
u} and the Planck mass M_P on the gravitational side of the field equation.
artifact.category_tag: Conformal gravity and dynamical mass generation
artifact.status_search_result: Mannheim and Kazanas's conformal (Weyl) gravity program proposes a concrete answer: replace the Einstein–Hilbert action with one quadratic in the Weyl tensor, so the gravitational side of the field equation is the (traceless) Bach tensor matched to a traceless dynamically-generated T_{\mu\nu}, with Newton's constant induced by spontaneous breaking of conformal symmetry. Subsequent work (e.g. Mannheim, "Making the Case for Conformal Gravity", Found. Phys. 2011) develops phenomenology (galactic rotation curves, cancellation of cosmological constant). However, conformal gravity remains controversial (issues with ghosts, solar-system limit, perturbations) and is not universally accepted as a complete resolution, so the broader question of how to reconcile Einstein gravity with dynamical mass generation and conformal matter is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Making the Case for Conformal Gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Conformal gravity retains the logical structure of general relativity but replaces the Einstein–Hilbert action by a quadratic contraction of the Weyl tensor; dynamical mass generation is compatible with a traceless T_{\mu\nu}.
status_evidence.claim: A concrete proposal addressing the question exists (Mannheim's conformal gravity program), making the problem partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Conformal Gravity: Dark Matter and Dark Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Dynamical interactions that produce elementary particle mass keep the total energy-momentum tensor traceless; conformal symmetry breaking induces Newton's constant and cancels the cosmological-constant contribution.
status_evidence.claim: Within the conformal gravity framework, dynamical mass generation is reconciled with tracelessness and a dynamical Planck scale.

status_evidence.title: Einstein gravity from Conformal Gravity in 6D
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study how Einstein gravity may emerge from conformal gravity.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between conformal and Einstein gravity remains an active research area, indicating the problem is not fully closed.
